title: 1989 AMC 8 Problem 18
statement: A calculator has a reciprocal key that replaces the number currently displayed with its reciprocal. For example, if the display shows \(4\) and the key is pressed, the display becomes \(0.25.\) If \(32\) is currently displayed, what is the fewest number of times the reciprocal key must be pressed so that the display again reads \(32?\)

solutions.text:
Pressing the key once changes \(32\) to its reciprocal \(\frac{1}{32}.\)

Pressing it a second time takes the reciprocal again, returning to \(\frac{1}{\frac{1}{32}} = 32.\) So \(2\) presses are enough.

Thus, the correct answer is B .
hints: Pressing the key once turns \(32\) into \(\frac{1}{32}\)
The reciprocal of the reciprocal of a number is the number itself
